title: Keeping steady time: the sleeping drummer
summary: Rene says he held time solidly and could play for hours asleep, and Russell mentions another musician who slept while playing.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: We'd get over, you see, when we'd get to playing waltzes and things like that, you might could hear some of them on that record. I had some of the off his beat, I don't know if it was, well, I had some off beats that could almost throw a man off, you see, but we were just used to that, you know, after effect, you see. And while my brother could play so good, I was considered as a man, held time like a cloud. Do you know I was the honest drummer? A fellow was talking about that down the day. You know the boy who played the trombone I was talking with when he was there on the Jackson Avenue by that church there?
I see, that was the young shell boy.

Yeah, yeah, well he can tell you, I was the honest man who never played a drum sleeping. I was solid, I was snowing. I was the honest man who played drums, then he slept for two hours. I was like, I'm a little bit of a drum, I never break that drum, I changed that time. See, I never changed that time. That's right, if they changed the walls, I stayed with the fox rod, I just changed like that, just changed like that, sleeping for two, three hours. And you hear me tell you, because them fellows used to come watch me. And I'd be snowing, they'd know I was sleeping. So that's what they're fighting for sleeping. I was a walking, sleeping drummer.
Somebody else I heard used to go to sleep playing drums, I can't think of.
